belief: Pastors and leaders are closer to God than I am.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that pastors and leaders are closer to God than you are, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Seeing leaders on a stage and feeling distant from them. Church cultures that treat clergy as a higher class of Christian. Feeling unqualified to pray or serve. Assuming that spiritual titles mean spiritual closeness. Your own sense of unworthiness.
teaches: All believers are a royal priesthood, a people belonging to God. Every Christian can approach the throne of grace with confidence. Jesus told His disciples that they have one Teacher and one Father, and that they are all brothers and sisters. Righteousness comes through faith in Jesus to all who believe, with no distinction. Leaders have important roles, but they are not closer to God by position. Your access to God is as full as theirs.
self_statements: Pastors have a special connection to God that I don’t.
God listens to leaders more than me.
I’m just an ordinary church member.
My prayers don’t count as much as theirs.
I need a leader to hear from God for me.
I’ll never be as close to God as they are.
errors: Measuring your closeness to God by someone else’s role.
Assuming a title means greater access to God.
Treating your relationship with God as second-class.
questions: What does 1 Peter 2:9 call all believers?
Who can approach God’s throne with confidence?
What did Jesus say about titles in Matthew 23?
Is there any distinction in how people are made right with God?
Does a leader’s role give them more access to God?
What does my own relationship with God look like?
How can I draw near to God today?
truth: Pastors and leaders are not closer to God than I am because of their role. I am part of a royal priesthood. Through Jesus, I can approach God’s throne with confidence. Leaders serve important roles, but we are all brothers and sisters with one Father and one Teacher. My access to God is full and free.
hw_questions: What does God call all believers?
What did Jesus say about titles?
Is there distinction in how we’re saved?
Does a role give more access to God?
How can I draw near to God today?
hw_truths: I am part of a royal priesthood.
I can approach God’s throne with confidence.
We all have one Father and one Teacher.
There is no distinction in Christ.
My access to God is full and free.
Leaders serve; they do not stand between me and God.
log: Each day, write one way I drew near to God myself.
name_example: But Sarah is chosen, a royal priest, holy, belonging to God, to proclaim the virtues of Him who called her out of darkness into His marvelous light.
actions: Spend ten minutes each day this week
talking to God yourself, without waiting for a leader.
and write what they say about your access to God.
Share something God has shown you
Thank a leader for their service,
remembering they are a brother or sister in Christ.
tracker: One way I drew near to God
prayer: Father, thank You that through Jesus I can come to You myself. Help me reject the lie that pastors and leaders are closer to You than I am. Thank You for making me part of a royal priesthood. Draw me near to You today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
